correctness.rationale: A cyclic detailed global-balance sum verifies the stationary Gibbs law; exact N/c binomial-composition count and uniform factorial-moment domination imply the limiting run count. Exact conditional vacancy gap probabilities yield E[B]=rho/(lambda N)+o(1/N), B higher falling moments O(N^-k); combining these with A<=C, q/N^2->lambda yields the moment hierarchy, variance and sharp burst frequency. Boundary cases rho=0,1, lambda=0,infinity and threshold exactly alpha lambda are excluded. A standalone finite-state enumeration and exact stationary balance verifier passed 2239 checks, not relied upon as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The source model proves Gibbs stationarity and an ordinary thermodynamic mean, and older Ising results cover the static domain-wall count. The newly assessed implication is the strongly singular joint N-rate scaling of the stationary configuration-dependent instantaneous jump intensity, including convergence in probability to zero with a positive mean, a linear variance, a complete fixed-moment hierarchy and order-1/N burst frequencies. Primary full texts and relevant research-record searches did not disclose that combined conclusion; absence of search hits is not taken as proof of priority. Broader implicit coverage remains an explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: Classical 1D Ising-domain wall combinatorics implies the static limiting block-count law, so its isolation is not novel.
Unsurveyed general rare-event theorems for singular-rate finite Markov chains may subsume the weighted burst-moment statement.
Only the ensemble of one-time instantaneous rates is studied, not dynamic shot noise or full counting statistics.

value.rationale: Strong follower recovery produces a new physically motivated singular regime, q comparable to N squared, which is precisely the crossover for one-site gaps within the few macroscopic runs of the canonical stationary gas. Typical snapshots then have negligible per-bond instantaneous transition intensity while rare O(1/N) snapshots maintain finite transport expectation and grow the variance linearly with system length; all fixed moments and rare-tail frequency are explicit. This resolves a nontrivial gap between mean current and typical instantaneous activity, not an arbitrary combinatorial slice.
